sections.text:
sync: wedge-fallback IBD candidate selection when no peer confirms
Contributed by Ziyang (as exfer-stack) upstream to ahuman-exfer/exfer, the Exfer chain itself.
This pull request is merged.
https://github.com/ahuman-exfer/exfer/pull/13

Closes the wedge surfaced by #12's diagnostic log on `exfer-node-stack` post-v1.11.1: 8 connected peers all report a current-mainnet tip and `cw_gt=true`, but `tip.confirmed=false` and `ever_confirmed_for_ibd=false` everywhere → `should_ibd` returns `None` for hours, chain only advances via opportunistic NewBlock gossip, never catches up the gap.

Root cause: catch-22 in the candidacy gate. `should_ibd` requires `tip.confirmed || ever_confirmed_for_ibd`. The former needs background tip validation to complete (deadlines exceeding on deep gaps); the latter requires `run_ibd Ok` which requires `should_ibd → Some` which... loops.

## Change A — wedge-fallback in `is_eligible_ibd_candidate`

When NO peer has been observed confirmed for the process lifetime AND the supervisor has been running ≥ `IBD_NO_CONFIRMED_FALLBACK_SECS = 600` (10 min), relax the gate to accept the highest-`cumulative_work` peer's claim even unconfirmed.

Eligibility is now a pure free function — extracted for unit-test coverage:

\`\`\`rust
fn is_eligible_ibd_candidate(
    tip_confirmed: bool,
    ever_confirmed_for_ibd: bool,
    cooldown_ok: bool,
    cw_better: bool,
    wedge_fallback_eligible: bool,
) -> bool {
    let confirmation_ok = tip_confirmed
        || ever_confirmed_for_ibd
        || (wedge_fallback_eligible && cw_better);
    confirmation_ok && cooldown_ok && cw_better
}
\`\`\`

Latches OFF as soon as any peer crosses `tip.confirmed=true` (state var `last_any_peer_confirmed: Option<Instant>` never re-arms within a process lifetime). Healthy nodes never enter the relaxed path.

## Change B — sticky-by-delivery on `run_ibd Ok`

Pairs with Change A: once the fallback path lets a first IBD complete, immediately flip the IBD peer's `ever_confirmed_for_ibd=true` so subsequent attempts use the normal sticky path. Without this, every IBD attempt would need to keep re-crossing the wedge fallback gate.

The legacy `if confirmed { lp.ever_confirmed_for_ibd = true; }` inside the post-IBD GetTip handler is left untouched — it remains an independent confirmation path and a no-op when this commit's earlier flip has already happened.

## Safety argument for relaxing confirmation

The strict gate was designed to prevent peers from making us waste resources IBDing a fake chain. The relaxation accepts unconfirmed claims, but:

1. Every block streamed inside `run_ibd` is PoW-validated at full Argon2id rate. A peer lying about cumulative_work gets cooldown'd as soon as their headers fail expected-difficulty or PoW.
2. `is_better_chain` still gates selection — peers claiming equal-or-worse work are filtered before reaching the fallback path.
3. Worst case: malicious peer claims massive work, ties up the IBD slot until their fake chain fails verification → 60 s cooldown + retry next peer. Same blast radius as today's "peer disconnects mid-IBD" case, no consensus damage.
